metadata.title: Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Developing Drugs for Treatment
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 22 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 23 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 24 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 25 not required. 26
candidates.context: This guidance is intended to provide recommendations to sponsors regarding eligibility criteria, 17 trial design considerations, and efficacy endpoints to enhance clinical trial data quality and to 18 foster greater efficiency in development programs for drugs for the treatment of neovascular 19 age-related macular degeneration. 2 , 3 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Division of Ophthalmology in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the Food and Drug Administration. For biological products regulated by CBER, sponsors should contact the Office of Tissues and Advanced Therapies (OTAT).

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration 33 should consider the following regarding trial design: 34
candidates.context: • FDA recommends parallel-group, randomized by patient, double-masked trials in which 36 the investigational drug group demonstrates superiority over the control group. 37

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration 47 should consider the following regarding comparative clinical trials: 48
candidates.context: • Each investigational drug arm is expected to have at least one other comparative arm in 50 which the dosing frequency, criterion for dosing adjustments, and criterion for 51 interventions are the same. 52

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration 116 should consider the following regarding safety: 117
candidates.context: E. Safety Considerations 114 • FDA recommends that approximately 400 or more patients using the investigational drug 119 complete treatment with a concentration of the investigational drug at least as high as 120 proposed for marketing and with a dosing frequency at least as frequent as proposed for 121 marketing. 122

candidates.statement: • Before submission of a marketing application, the sponsor should ensure that at least 300 124 patients have completed at least 9 months of follow-up after the initiation of treatment. 125

candidates.statement: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration rarely occurs in the pediatric population. Sponsors 161 should consider pediatric assessment waiver requests when submitting their required pediatric 162 study plans under the Pediatric Research Equity Act. 12
candidates.context: 12 See section 505B(e)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic (FD&C) Act (21 U.S.C. 355c(e)(1)) and section 505B(a)(1)(A) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355c(a)(1)(A)).
